title: Numeric & optimization — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: The most rigorously measured module in the library — P0–P7 complete, ~1,827 assertions, every parallel route gated by a measured threshold and every kernel bit-identical under threads. It leads with something NumPy has no concept of: exactness — an arbitrary-precision numeric tower (bignum, exact rational, money-exact decimal) with a register that tells you why a value is exact or not. On dense linear algebra it reaches LAPACK-tier decompositions, and it ships reverse-mode autodiff with L-BFGS. It is deliberately "not a NumPy": no broadcasting, raw matmul peak below tuned BLAS, and it refuses what it cannot measure a use for.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. Uniquely here, several "gaps" are documented, measured refusals — a discipline worth reading as such, called out in the honesty note below.

lanes.engine: An arbitrary-precision tower over `std.math.big`: bignum, exact rationals, and money-exact decimal (scaled integers, so `0.1+0.2` is exactly `0.3`), plus a full number-theory set. An exactness register — `IsExact()`, `Why()`, `Representation()` — reports why a value is exact or approximate.
lanes.owed: A genuine differentiator: NumPy has no exactness concept at all. The 2⁷³ f64 boundary is handled by storing the value as a string and routing arithmetic away from the float path.

lanes.engine: `matrix.zig` + `linalg.zig`: matmul (i-k-j SIMD + threaded), determinant via LU, `Solve`, `Inverse`, `LeastSquares`, `PseudoInverse` (Penrose-4 verified), rank, condition number — all engine-backed and checked against NumPy.
lanes.owed: Core dense LA is at parity for correctness. Raw throughput is the ceiling, not coverage — see lane 12.

lanes.engine: Symmetric eigen (Jacobi) and — the hard part — general non-symmetric eigen in `eigen_general.zig`: Parlett-Reinsch balancing, Householder→Hessenberg, Francis double-shift QR, Schur forms. Plus one-sided-Jacobi SVD, Householder QR, Cholesky, and polynomial roots via companion matrix.
lanes.owed: The decomposition set is LAPACK-tier and genuinely hard to get right — general eigen with a Francis QR is not something most libraries hand-roll correctly. At parity for the analyst's needs.

lanes.engine: Reverse-mode autodiff (`autodiff.zig`, a compiled tape) with `valueAndGradient`, and L-BFGS with a bracket-and-zoom strong-Wolfe line search (`lbfgs.zig`). Verified against hand-derived gradients to 8–12 decimals; Rosenbrock converges in 34 iterations.
lanes.owed: Reverse-mode AD plus a real quasi-Newton optimizer is a strong, uncommon pairing in a general library. The optimizer returns a full record (status, iterations, `Why()`).

lanes.engine: The discipline is the product: SIMD + row-banded threaded matmul (16× cache reorder, +19% vector, up to 7× threaded), Neumaier compensated summation (2.5×), and a residency model where the engine copy is truth — resident reductions run 19× faster. Every route is admitted only above a measured `calib.Gate` threshold, and results are bit-identical under threads.
lanes.owed: Raw single-thread matmul peaks ~15 GFLOP/s — below a tuned BLAS — because there is no MKL/OpenBLAS binding. The rigor is category-leading; the raw ceiling is not.

lanes.engine: `stzNumBuffer` over `numbuf.zig` — a contiguous, engine-owned f64 buffer with `dot`, `scale`, `add/sub/mul` and reductions (sum/mean/variance/stddev) that never marshal. The residency keystone.
lanes.owed: Deliberately "not a NumPy": no broadcasting, no fancy indexing, no dtype algebra, no n-D arrays. A 1-D f64 workhorse, not a tensor library — multi-dimensional tensors live in the Neural tier.

lanes.engine: Real LP/MIP: an engine simplex (`simplex.zig`, measured 41× after a cubic re-parse fix) with a branch-and-bound integer tier, driven from a modelling DSL (`stzOptimModel`) and an exact coefficient compiler (no `eval()`), plus a natural-language sentence surface to the same AST and a `.zopt` file round-trip.
lanes.owed: No interior-point method, no large-scale MIP (HiGHS deliberately not vendored) and no QP (OSQP refused — no consumer). A capable modelling+solve surface, not an industrial solver.

lanes.engine: `special.zig`: erf/erfc, log-gamma and gamma, incomplete gamma and beta as workhorses, and the Normal/t/χ²/F distribution CDFs and quantiles that power the statistics plane.
lanes.owed: Testing-focused. The wider GSL catalogue — Bessel, Airy, elliptic, hypergeometric — is absent (no consumer yet). No dedicated `stzNumber` special-function face.

lanes.engine: `solver.zig`: linear and quadratic roots, bisection, Newton, Simpson integration, polynomial evaluation, and the interpolation helpers (lerp / clamp / map-range). `stzPolynomial` and `stzMathFunction` sit on top.
lanes.owed: Basic: no adaptive quadrature, no ODE/BVP solvers, no multi-dimensional root finding — the standard GSL/SciPy fare beyond single-variable roots and fixed-rule integration.

lanes.engine: `random.zig` over Zig's Xoshiro / PCG / ChaCha generators: seeded ints, floats, Gaussian, exponential, bulk-n variants, shuffle, Bernoulli and weighted choice, under one `SeedRandom` authority.
lanes.owed: Good generators, but a narrow distribution set next to NumPy's Generator — no binomial, Poisson, gamma, beta or Dirichlet samplers yet.

lanes.engine: `fft.zig`: radix-2 Cooley-Tukey with the NumPy `fft`/`ifft` convention, plus `convolveReal`, magnitudes, phases, power spectrum and dominant-bin detection.
lanes.owed: Radix-2 only — non-power-of-2 sizes, a real-optimized `rfft`, and multi-dimensional transforms are all missing. Fine for the current spectral consumers, short of a general FFT.

lanes.engine: `complex.zig`: arithmetic, modulus (hypot), argument, conjugate, principal square root and exp, with division via Smith's formula for numerical stability. Surfaced as `stzComplex` and in `ComplexEigenValues()`.
lanes.owed: Deliberately partial: no log, inverse-trig or general powers — a stated branch-cut policy plus no current consumer. Enough for eigenvalues, not for complex analysis.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first two close genuine capability gaps; the third is throughput and breadth that partly runs against the module's stated "not a NumPy" philosophy — flagged as optional.

items.title: Arbitrary-N & multi-dimensional FFT
items.text: Beyond radix-2: mixed-radix / Bluestein for non-power-of-2 sizes, a real-optimized `rfft`, and 2-D transforms. This is table stakes against NumPy/FFTW and the clearest owed item in the compute set.

items.title: Complete the complex surface
items.text: Log, inverse-trig and general powers with a stated branch-cut convention. Today complex is "enough for eigenvalues"; a consumer needing complex analysis or signal work hits the wall immediately.

items.title: Adaptive quadrature + an ODE stepper
items.text: Adaptive Gauss-Kronrod integration and a Runge-Kutta ODE solver over the existing `solver.zig` — the standard GSL/SciPy toolkit the roots lane stops just short of.

items.title: Broaden the sampling distributions
items.text: Binomial, Poisson, gamma, beta and Dirichlet samplers over the existing generators — small additions that close the gap to NumPy's `Generator` and directly feed the statistics plane's resampling gap.

items.title: Feature standardization for the trainer
items.text: The pinned issue: logistic regression diverges on unscaled features. Wiring standardization into the trainer is a small, known fix that removes a documented sharp edge.

tiers.title: Tier C — strategic (and partly against the stated philosophy)

items.title: A tuned BLAS path for raw throughput
items.text: An MKL/OpenBLAS binding (or a GPU f32 route) would lift matmul from ~15 GFLOP/s toward tuned peak. Runs against "not a NumPy," so worth it only if numeric throughput becomes a first-class goal.

items.title: The GSL special-function catalogue
items.text: Bessel, Airy, elliptic and hypergeometric functions. Currently absent for want of a consumer — add them when a consumer (physics, signal, advanced stats) actually arrives.

items.title: QP & industrial-scale MIP
items.text: Quadratic programming (OSQP-class) and large-scale MIP (HiGHS-class), both refused today for lack of a consumer. Strategic if the optimization plane grows past modelling-and-solve.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: Verification here is unusually strong: P0–P7 complete, ~1,827 numeric assertions checked against a NumPy reference oracle (decompositions to 8–12 decimals, matmul bit-identical across the reorder and across threads). Crucially, many "gaps" are deliberate, measured refusals recorded as results — elementwise multicore killed (PCIe / memory wall), GPU f64 refused (1/64-rate silicon), `mpdecimal` / OSQP / HiGHS / KISS FFT not built "because nothing calls them." Read those as discipline, not as a to-do list.

Softanza's numeric foundation trades NumPy's breadth for exactness, correctness and measured discipline: an arbitrary-precision exact tower NumPy lacks, LAPACK-tier decompositions with reverse-mode autodiff, and a residency-and-gating model where nothing parallel ships without a measurement. Its real distance from the top is raw BLAS throughput and a general FFT — everything else it's missing, it's missing on purpose.
